physical.notes: The company filed a criminal report on June 4, 2026; theft not confirmed and the device has not been found.

unknown.notes: Whoever removed the SSD is not identified. The device was in an unlocked cabinet in a server room that requires ID card plus biometric entry; 57 employees from 10 contractor companies entered the room between April 27 and May 26 (Asahi). Could be an insider, a contractor (partner) or an outsider; no source says.

asset.notes: Palm-size external SSD used as a temporary backup device.

plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/23333
Template Physical-ext-theft-udev used as scaffold (Physical Theft, availability Loss, data_disclosure Potentially, one-step chain). Deviations: (1) Actor coded actor.unknown instead of External/Unaffiliated/Financial: nobody has been identified, and the only people known to have entered the access-controlled server room in the window were 57 workers from 10 contractor companies, so the actor may be internal, partner or external. No motive source. (2) Asset M - Disk drive (portable SSD backup device), not U - Desktop or laptop; physical vector Victim secure area. (3) Discovery coded partner/Other: Asahi says the contractor worker who made the backup found it missing when he returned on May 26 (BleepingComputer just says IT staff); template default is internal/Reported by employee. (4) Added a cp event to the chain because confidentiality is coded.
Theft vs. loss: the company filed a criminal report (June 4) for suspected theft but has not concluded the SSD was stolen; its final report only says whereabouts unknown. A reviewer may prefer Error Loss (internal/partner, Carelessness). The final report blames four management failures (no approval process for external media, no instruction to lock the cabinet, no encryption/password, no written contractor instructions), but under VERIS those are control failures, not a separate Error action, so none was coded.
Data: final report (July 8, 2026, via rocket-boys.co.jp) raised the count from 10.9M to up to 13.54M records: 10.03M individuals (Personal) and 3.51M corporate/other entities (coded Other, customer business records incl. ~1.46M streetlight/traffic-signal contracts). Fields: names, supply-site addresses, electricity usage, retailer names, supply point IDs; phone numbers only for switching-system records. No bank, card or email data. SSD was not encrypted or password-protected (final report; Asahi) -> Stored unencrypted. data_disclosure Potentially: no evidence of leakage found (the company monitored flea-market sites and the web).
Timeline: last seen April 27, 2026 after the backup; found missing May 26. The removal happened sometime in that window; incident date set to April 27 (start of window). Discovery up to about 4 weeks -> Weeks. dbir_year 2027.
Victim: the T&D subsidiary (Kyushu Electric Power Transmission and Distribution Co.) owns the data and made the announcement; some press names the parent Kyushu Electric Power. NAICS refined from the issue's 221 to 2211 (power generation, transmission and distribution); the subsidiary does both transmission and distribution, so no single 6-digit code fits. Employee count 1001 to 10000 is inferred: Mynavi lists 11,888 employees combined for the parent and the T&D subsidiary (FY2024); the subsidiary alone is a part of that. Region Eastern Asia (142030).
Sources: Asahi (issue link; site blocked to fetch, quoted text in issue used), BleepingComputer, CyberInsider, teiss, rocket-boys.co.jp (final report summary).

event_chain.summary: SSD taken from unlocked cabinet in server room (suspected theft)
Unencrypted customer data out of victim possession

summary: Kyushu Electric Power Transmission and Distribution Co. (a Kyushu Electric Power subsidiary) lost an unencrypted, non-password-protected portable SSD holding customer data. On April 27, 2026 a contractor backed up customer data to the SSD and left it in an unlocked cabinet inside the company's access-controlled server room; on May 26 it was found missing. The company filed a criminal report for suspected theft on June 4 and disclosed the incident on June 8. The device has not been found. Its July 8 final report put the scope at up to 13.54 million records (10.03 million individuals and 3.51 million corporate and other entities): names, supply addresses, electricity usage, retailer names, supply point IDs and, for some, phone numbers.

victim.victim_id: Kyushu Electric Power Transmission and Distribution Co., Inc.
